links.reason: The passage shows training and deploying an XGBoost model for inference, but it does not indicate that the model artifact is self-contained with preprocessing and prediction components bundled together.

links.label: Hypothesis-driven experimentation
links.description: Short feedback cycles and explicit hypotheses guide experiments, learning, and backlog decisions.
links.reason: The passage supports fast iteration and daily user feedback, but it does not explicitly describe explicit hypotheses guiding experiments or backlog decisions.

links.label: Dedicated feature engineering pipeline
links.description: A distinct pipeline selects, transforms, combines, and prepares raw data before algorithm use.
links.reason: It explicitly describes separating the code that fetches data, trains models, and validates results into orchestrated DAG components before production use.

links.label: Time- and event-triggered training
links.description: Schedulers, calendar events, messages, monitoring events, or data and code changes initiate training.
links.reason: The passage explicitly says the pipeline is automatically executed in production based on a schedule or in response to a trigger, which matches time- and event-triggered training.

links.label: Managed cloud MLOps platform
links.description: Adopt a fully managed cloud platform spanning substantial portions of model development and operations.
links.reason: The passage discusses building custom MLOps with multiple tools and microservices, but it does not describe adopting a fully managed cloud MLOps platform.

links.label: User-defined dataset validation
links.description: Custom routines detect inconsistencies, incorrect associations, missing values, and other data errors.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes user-defined data validation routines that detect inconsistencies, wrong associations, and missing values.

links.label: Dedicated feature engineering pipeline
links.description: A distinct pipeline selects, transforms, combines, and prepares raw data before algorithm use.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes a data engineering pipeline that cleans, transforms, and prepares data to create training and testing datasets for ML algorithms.

links.label: Three-way prediction input contract
links.description: Supply predictions with model artifacts, processed data, and fresh live signals.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes three kinds of inputs—models, data, and fresh signals from live services—matching the three-way prediction input contract.

links.label: Schema-anomaly pipeline halt
links.description: Stop training or processing when incoming features are unexpected, missing, or invalid.
links.reason: The passage supports automatic schema/domain validation of incoming data, but it does not explicitly say the pipeline halts when features are unexpected, missing, or invalid.

links.label: Automated retraining-and-deployment pipeline
links.description: Pipeline automation that retrains, validates, and deploys models from offline development.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes an ML pipeline that automates retraining and deployment, matching the value.

links.label: Neural architecture search
links.description: Automated search selects neural architectures using defined spaces, metrics, and search algorithms.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes NAS as automated search over architectures using search spaces, evaluation metrics, and algorithms.

links.label: Batch and real-time processing support
links.description: Accommodate both batch and real-time execution modes in the ML processing architecture.
links.reason: The passage explicitly says a production-ready ML system should support both batch and real-time processing.

links.label: Offline batch training
links.description: Training runs as an offline process rather than during prediction requests.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes offline computation as a batch-like process for precomputing results rather than responding during requests.

links.label: Notebook-based prototyping
links.description: Data scientists prototype with notebooks despite an enterprise-provided platform.
links.reason: The passage discusses using Jupyter notebooks for initial data exploration and prototyping, but it does not mention an enterprise-provided platform or explicitly contrast notebooks with one.

links.label: Centralized consistent storage
links.description: Accessible data is retained in a consistent structure, ideally in one centralized location.
links.reason: It explicitly says data should be stored in a consistent structure and conveniently in one place, matching centralized consistent storage.

links.label: Multi-language implementation support
links.description: Use infrastructure that permits services or ML components to be implemented in multiple programming languages.
links.reason: The passage discusses letting data scientists use code in their chosen language and contrasts it with forcing porting to R, but it does not explicitly describe a multi-language implementation infrastructure.

links.label: Containerized prediction microservice
links.description: A prediction model is packaged and deployed as a containerized microservice.
links.reason: The passage explicitly says OpenWhisk supports containers and describes deep-learning microservices deployed as small code components in orchestrated sequences.

links.label: Automated ML lifecycle management
links.description: Automate training, deployment, retraining, and related lifecycle operations to reduce manual effort.
links.reason: The passage explicitly says MLOps automates the ML lifecycle from training to deployment and retraining, which matches automated lifecycle management.

links.label: Microservice architecture
links.description: Clearly separated product components are independently served as microservices.
links.reason: The passage explicitly says they use a serverless or microservice architecture with separate microservices handling stream analysis and drift detection.

links.label: Single-objective error minimization
links.description: Considering one error objective instead of broader operational criteria was rejected for model assessment.
links.reason: The passage says you cannot simply blend broader criteria into an error minimization goal and must consider other ongoing oversight criteria instead.

links.label: Local-machine data access
links.description: Develop by accessing protected data directly from a local machine.
links.reason: The passage contrasts this option by saying local-machine data access was not allowed and that they used VMs instead, which indirectly relates to the rejected status.

links.label: Software-metrics-only monitoring
links.description: Rely exclusively on software metrics to monitor a production model.
links.reason: The passage explicitly says that looking only at software metrics is too little, which rejects software-metrics-only monitoring.

links.label: Direct underlying-data access
links.description: Allowing direct access to underlying data was explicitly rejected as an infrastructure access approach.
links.reason: The passage explicitly says organizations do not want too many users having direct access to the underlying data, which matches the rejected infrastructure access approach.

links.label: Business-KPI-only monitoring
links.description: Wait exclusively for downstream product or business KPIs to monitor model behavior.
links.reason: It explicitly says looking only at downstream product or business KPIs is too late, rejecting exclusive reliance on them.

links.label: Active model performance monitoring
links.description: The source explicitly rejected active model-performance monitoring as the selected monitoring approach.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that MLOps level 0 lacks active performance monitoring and does not track or log predictions, matching a rejection of active model-performance monitoring.

links.label: Avoided repeated notebook computation
links.description: Avoid repeated expensive training, retrieval, or database computation through cached results.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes Jupyter caching cell results to avoid rerunning expensive training, downloads, and database queries.

links.label: Improved transformation code quality
links.description: A structured development environment improves the quality of transformation code.
links.reason: The passage says event-stream teams follow a higher standard for data quality and documentation, but it does not specifically claim that a structured development environment improves transformation code quality.

links.label: Managed platform flexibility and scalability
links.description: Flexibility and scalability resulting from using a fully managed platform.
links.reason: It explicitly describes SageMaker as a fully managed end-to-end cloud ML platform that enables developers to create, train, and deploy models, which implies managed-platform flexibility and scalability.

links.label: Production accuracy requirement
links.description: Require AutoML-produced models to meet the accuracy needed for real-world use.
links.reason: The passage says training seeks the best accuracy and validation checks the model is working, but it does not explicitly require AutoML-produced models to meet a real-world production accuracy threshold.

links.label: Partial monitoring coverage
links.description: Only a minority of deployed models receive monitoring, leaving substantial operational blind spots.
links.reason: It mentions lack of active performance monitoring, but not that only a minority of deployed models are monitored.

links.label: Model degradation
links.description: Changing real-world data causes predictive performance to decline over time.
links.reason: The passage explicitly says live data changes cause model degradation and predictive performance to decrease over time.

links.label: Duplicated notebook queries
links.description: Repeated notebook query cells create duplicated query code.
links.reason: The passage explicitly says notebook cell magic can force users to duplicate similar queries, describing duplicated query code as an outcome.

links.label: Data-type mismatch detection
links.description: Observed validation output identifying inputs whose types violate dataset expectations.
links.reason: The passage explicitly reports a datatype_check violation from Model Monitor, which is validation output indicating a type mismatch against expectations.

links.label: Replicable IDE code development
links.description: Use an IDE setup that supports proper, repeatable code and results.
links.reason: It explicitly recommends identical dependencies and the same technical stack in dev and production, plus reproducible results via containers or virtual machines.

links.label: Notebook showcasing and exploratory workflow
links.description: Use interactive notebooks for presenting results and conducting exploratory data analysis.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes Jupyter/IPython Notebook as a web-based interactive environment for scientific computing and data analysis with inline plots and rich media.
